answers.children: Kerry Blue Terriers are moderately good with children when the children are older. Their medium build and high energy suit active play with older kids yet their spirited nature and protective instincts can lead to them knocking smaller children over during zoomies; the breed's farm-dog history of guarding and herding also influences how they interact with little ones. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 6/10)
answers.other-pets: Kerry Blue Terriers do not always get along with other pets. Their vermin-hunting background gives them strong prey drive towards small animals while their dominant streak often creates tension with other dogs especially of the same sex; spirited and protective instincts further shape these interactions.
answers.exercise: Kerry Blue Terriers need at least one hour of vigorous daily exercise. Bred as all-purpose Irish farm dogs for hunting vermin and herding they thrive on brisk walks runs in fenced areas and challenging games of fetch; without enough activity their intelligence and energy turn into destructive digging and chewing.
answers.shedding: Kerry Blue Terriers shed very little year-round. Their medium curly single coat lacks the heavy undercoat of many breeds so loose hair stays trapped in the curls rather than covering furniture although regular grooming is still required to prevent matting; the striking blue-gray texture demands consistent care to stay tidy.
answers.hypoallergenic: The Kerry Blue Terrier has a medium-length curly coat that sheds very little and produces minimal loose hair around the home. Its soft, wavy fur requires frequent brushing and professional grooming to prevent matting, particularly behind the ears and on the legs where the texture tangles easily. While no breed is genuinely hypoallergenic, this terrier is among those often suggested to allergy sufferers because of its low shedding (PawLabs shedding score: 2/10).
answers.training: Kerry Blue Terriers are not the easiest dogs to train. Their high intelligence makes them quick to learn but stubbornness and strong will from their independent farm-dog heritage mean they often test boundaries; spirited temperament requires patient consistent handling to channel their protective instincts productively.
answers.lifespan: Kerry Blue Terriers live 12-15 years. Their medium size and versatile build from Irish farm work support this range although health robustness varies with the individual; spirited energetic nature helps them stay active well into later years when given proper outlets for their intelligence.
answers.size: Kerry Blue Terriers reach 33-40 lb and stand 17-19 in tall. This compact yet sturdy medium build feels solid and substantial in the home without being overwhelming; their muscular frame from vermin hunting and herding gives them surprising strength for their height.
answers.barking: Kerry Blue Terriers bark a moderate amount. Their protective instincts and history as Irish farm guards lead them to alert at strangers delivery drivers or unusual sounds while their spirited independent nature means they rarely bark without reason once the perceived threat passes.
answers.apartment: Kerry Blue Terriers can live in an apartment with careful management. Their adaptable nature allows them to settle indoors when given sufficient exercise yet their moderate barking from protective instincts and high energy can disturb neighbours if mental stimulation or daily runs are neglected.
answers.first-time: Kerry Blue Terriers are not ideal as a first dog. Their stubborn strong-willed temperament and dominance with other dogs demand an experienced handler who can channel the breed's intelligence and protective instincts; first-time owners may struggle with the spirited independence bred into these Irish terriers.
